
This workflow is for analyzing data from high-throughput phenotype screens. The images from these screens were processed with phenotypic. The metrics were then saved at Phenotypic_metrics.csv. 

The order of this workflow is: 
  1. Morphology Filters
  2. IQR Outlier Filters 
  3. Filtering Patterns  
  4. Edge Effect Analysis 
  5. Coefficient of Variation Analysis 
  6. Pearson's R 

Libraries
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)      
library(broom)          
library(ggpointdensity) 
library(scales)
```

Set your filtering parameters
```{r}
circularity_parameter = 0.7 
solidity_parameter=7.5 
compactness_parameter=2.5 
iqr_fence = 1.5
```

load in data files 
```{r}
#this is the raw data from phenotypic 
raw_data <- read.csv("input/phenotypic_data.csv")
```

*Start of Filtering Pipeline for Raw Data* 
Morphological Filters 
What will this do? It'll create a new column called "Filter" that will tell you if the data passed or didn't, and if it didn't pass, why it didn't pass (e.g. it didn't pass the circularity filter so it says "Circularity")
```{r}
raw_data_1 <- raw_data %>% 
  mutate(
    # Create individual failure flags using the new column names
    fail_circ  = if_else(!is.na(Circularity) & Circularity <= circularity_parameter, "Circularity", ""),
    fail_solid = if_else(!is.na(Solidity) & Solidity <= solidity_parameter, "Solidity", ""),
    fail_comp  = if_else(!is.na(Compactness) & Compactness >= compactness_parameter, "Compactness", "")
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    # Combine failures separated by " & "
    Filter = paste(fail_circ, fail_solid, fail_comp, sep = " & ") %>% 
      # Clean up leading, trailing, or double ampersands
      str_replace_all("^[ &]+|[ &]+$", "") %>% 
      str_replace_all(" &  & ", " & ") %>% 
      str_trim(),
    # If empty, it passed all thresholds -> "TRUE"
    Filter = if_else(Filter == "", "Passed", Filter)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-fail_circ, -fail_solid, -fail_comp)

raw_data_1
```

IQR Outlier Filters
What will this do? We write a function to group data points according to the condition, set, time and strain, then remove any outliers using IQR. E.g. this will look at all replicates of strain 1 on Set 1 at time point 12 hr on glucose and determine if any of the replicates are an outlier. 
```{r}
#IQR Function 
iqr_outlier <- function(x, fence = 1.0) {
  q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr_val <- q3 - q1
  x >= (q1 - fence * iqr_val) & x <= (q3 + fence * iqr_val)
}
metric_cols <- c("Area")

#Apply the IQR Function to your dataset 
filtered_data <- raw_data_1 %>%
  group_by(Condition, Set, Time, Strain) %>% 
  mutate(
    passes_iqr = if_all(all_of(metric_cols), ~ iqr_outlier(.x, fence = iqr_fence)),
      Filter = case_when(
      passes_iqr ~ Filter,                               
      Filter == "TRUE" ~ "IQR",                          
      TRUE ~ paste0(Filter, "_IQR")                     
    )) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-passes_iqr) %>% 
  ungroup()

write.csv(filtered_data,"input/filtered_data.csv")
```

Filtering Patterns  

Now that filtering is finished, let's look at what was filtered out and where. This will give you the total data counts for the data points that passed and those that didn't, and why, as well as percentages. 
```{r}
filtered_data %>%
  mutate(
    #simplify the filtering conditions 
    Filter_Cleaned = case_when(
      str_detect(Filter, "Circularity") ~ "Circularity",
      str_detect(Filter, "Solidity")    ~ "Solidity",
      TRUE ~ as.character(Filter)
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(Filter_Cleaned) %>%
  #count how many times something was filtered 
  summarise(Count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  #add a percentage
  mutate(Percentage = round((Count / sum(Count)) * 100, 2))
```

For each condition, how did the filtering rates apply? For example, was more filtered out in xylose than pectin? 
```{r}
# Define custom carbon source order
carbon_order <- c("Pectin", "Lactose", "Cellobiose", "Galactose", "Xylose", "Arabinose", "30C")

Filtering_by_Condition <- filtered_data %>%
  # 1. Clean and standardize Filter category names
  mutate(
    Filter_Cleaned = case_when(
      Filter == "Passed" ~ "Retained Data Points",
      str_detect(Filter, "Circularity") ~ "Circularity Filtered",
      str_detect(Filter, "Solidity")    ~ "Solidity Filtered",
      str_detect(Filter, "IQR")         ~ "IQR Filtered",
      TRUE ~ as.character(Filter)
    )
  ) %>%
  # 2. Count total data points per Carbon Source and Filter Category
  group_by(Condition, Filter_Cleaned) %>%
  summarise(Count = n()/1000, .groups = "drop") %>%
  
  # 3. Pivot into wide format (one row per Carbon Source)
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Filter_Cleaned,
    values_from = Count,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  
  # 4. Select and reorder columns explicitly
  dplyr::select(
    `Carbon Source`        = Condition,
    `Retained Data Points` = matches("Retained Data Points"),
    `Circularity Filtered` = matches("Circularity Filtered"),
    `Solidity Filtered`    = matches("Solidity Filtered"),
    `IQR Filtered`         = matches("IQR Filtered")
  ) %>%
  
  # 5. Order rows from top to bottom by specified carbon source order
  mutate(`Carbon Source` = factor(`Carbon Source`, levels = carbon_order)) %>%
  arrange(`Carbon Source`) %>%
  mutate(`Carbon Source` = as.character(`Carbon Source`)) # Convert back to character for clean CSV export

# Display table
Filtering_by_Condition

# Export to CSV
write.csv(Filtering_by_Condition, "output/filtering_by_condition.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

Was the rate of filtering the same across all time points or different? 
```{r}
# Create contingency table: Time Point vs. Outlier/Filter Status
time_table <- table(filtered_data$Time, filtered_data$Filter %in% c("Passed"))

# Run Chi-Square Test
chisq_time <- chisq.test(time_table)
print(chisq_time)

# Inspect Observed vs Expected counts to identify early vs late patterns
chisq_time$observed
chisq_time$expected

# 1. Calculate percentage of filtered-out data per condition and time point
filtered_data %>%
  group_by(Time) %>%
  summarize(
    total_colonies = n(),
    filtered_count = sum(!Filter %in% c("Passed"), na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_filtered   = (filtered_count / total_colonies) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Were the colonies that were flagged unique or repeats? 
```{r}
# 1. Sort data temporally and flag consecutive failures per physical colony
repeat_failure_analysis <- filtered_data %>%
  mutate(Is_Fail = !Filter %in% c("Passed")) %>%
  arrange(Condition, Strain, Biological_Replicate,Technical_Replicate, Time) %>%
  group_by(Condition, Strain, Biological_Replicate,Technical_Replicate) %>%
  mutate(
    # Check if the colony failed at the NEXT available time point
    Failed_Next_Timepoint = lead(Is_Fail),
    Has_Next_Timepoint = !is.na(lead(Is_Fail))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# 2. Filter down to only instances where a failure occurred (Is_Fail == TRUE)
failure_events <- repeat_failure_analysis %>%
  filter(Is_Fail == TRUE & Has_Next_Timepoint == TRUE)

# 3. Calculate global repeat failure rate
repeat_rate <- mean(failure_events$Failed_Next_Timepoint) * 100

cat(sprintf("Total failure events evaluated: %d\n", nrow(failure_events)))
cat(sprintf("Repeat failure rate: %.2f%% of failed colonies failed again at the subsequent time point.\n", repeat_rate))
```

Get the binned counts for your circularity and solidity parameters for Figure 5a and 5b
```{r}
bin_metric_zero <- function(data, col_name, start, end, bin) {
  breaks <- round(seq(start, end, by = bin), 6)
  data %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[col_name]])) %>%
    mutate(
      # Assign into left-closed intervals [start, start + bin)
      Bin_Start = cut(
        .data[[col_name]], 
        breaks = breaks, 
        right = FALSE, 
        include.lowest = TRUE,
        labels = breaks[-length(breaks)]
      ),
      # Convert back to rounded numeric
      Bin_Start = round(as.numeric(as.character(Bin_Start)), 4)
    ) %>%
    # Filter out any points strictly falling outside [start, end]
    filter(!is.na(Bin_Start)) %>%
    count(Bin_Start, name = "Count") %>%
    # Fill in missing empty bins with 0 count across the clean breaks
    complete(
      Bin_Start = breaks[-length(breaks)], 
      fill = list(Count = 0)
    ) %>%
    mutate(Metric = col_name) %>%
    arrange(Bin_Start) %>%
    dplyr::select(Metric, Bin_Start, Count)
}

# Run pipeline (using your new df and column names)
df_binned <- bind_rows(
  bin_metric_zero(filtered_data, "Circularity", 0, 1, 0.025),
  bin_metric_zero(filtered_data, "Solidity", 0, 23, 0.5)
)

df_binned$Count = df_binned$Count/1000
write.csv(df_binned,"output/df_binned.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

Edge Effect Analysis 
We know where the negative controls are, so label the colonies for each set as surrounded vs peripheral. Then, test if there's a significant difference using Welch's T-Test 
```{r}
#Define negative control coordinates per Metadata_Set
neg_controls <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Set, ~row, ~col,
  1, 3, 3,  1, 2, 11, 1, 5, 9,  1, 7, 5,
  2, 2, 2,  2, 4, 6,  2, 6, 9,  2, 7, 4, 2, 7, 11,
  3, 2, 4,  3, 2, 9,  3, 6, 2,  3, 6, 10
)

#Build theoretical layout (excluding negative controls)
occupied_lookup <- tidyr::crossing(
  Set = c(1, 2, 3),
  row = 1:8,
  col = 1:12
) %>%
  anti_join(neg_controls, by = c("Set", "row", "col")) %>%
  mutate(grid_coords = paste(row, col, sep = "_")) %>%
  group_by(Set) %>%
  summarize(valid_coords = list(grid_coords), .groups = "drop")

# Generate master 96-well grid template with labels pre-assigned
master_grid_template <- tidyr::crossing(
  Set = c(1, 2, 3),
  row = 1:8,
  col = 1:12
) %>%
  mutate(Grid_Number = (row - 1) * 12 + col) %>%
  left_join(occupied_lookup, by = "Set") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    is_outer_border = (row == 1 | row == 8 | col == 1 | col == 12),
    has_top   = paste(row - 1, col, sep = "_") %in% valid_coords,
    has_bot   = paste(row + 1, col, sep = "_") %in% valid_coords,
    has_left  = paste(row, col - 1, sep = "_") %in% valid_coords,
    has_right = paste(row, col + 1, sep = "_") %in% valid_coords,
    
    is_neg_control = !paste(row, col, sep = "_") %in% valid_coords,
    
    Colony_Label_Template = case_when(
      is_neg_control ~ "negative_control",
      !is_outer_border & (has_top & has_bot & has_left & has_right) ~ "surrounded",
      TRUE ~ "edge"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(Set, Grid_Number, row, col, Colony_Label_Template)

# Safely calculate coordinates in filtered_data and join with master template
labeled_df <- filtered_data %>%
  mutate(
    Grid_Number = as.integer(Grid_Number),
    row = (Grid_Number - 1) %/% 12 + 1,
    col = (Grid_Number - 1) %% 12 + 1
  ) %>%
  # Full join to retain experimental data while ensuring dropped grid points exist
  full_join(
    master_grid_template,
    by = c("Set", "Grid_Number", "row", "col")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Use template assignment for all rows (including dropped ones)
    Colony_Label = Colony_Label_Template
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-Colony_Label_Template)

#Render 96-well array plot for each set to verify 
master_grid_template %>%
  filter(Set == 2) %>% ggplot(aes(x = col, y = row, fill = Colony_Label_Template)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Grid_Number), size = 3, color = "black") +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = 1:8, labels = LETTERS[1:8]) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, position = "top") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "edge" = "#E69F00", 
      "surrounded" = "#56B4E9", 
      "negative_control" = "#D55E00"
    ),
    labels = c(
      "edge" = "Edge (Peripheral)", 
      "surrounded" = "Surrounded", 
      "negative_control" = "Negative Control"
    )
  ) +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Column",
    y = "Row",
    fill = "Well Classification"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank()
  )
```

Now that we know which rows are edge vs surrounded, let's perform the edge effect test
```{r}
#Generate the dataset for the t-test
ttest_data <- labeled_df %>% 
  # Filter out negative controls and metrics that didn't pass the Filter test, as these will skew the results since they aren't real colonies 
  filter(
    Filter == "Passed",
    Colony_Label %in% c("edge", "surrounded"),
    !is.na(Area)
  ) 

#run the t-test
ttest_results = ttest_data %>% 
  #group by the condition, set, time and replicates. 
  group_by(Condition, Set, Time, Biological_Replicate, Technical_Replicate) %>%
  # Ensure at least 2 non-NA measurements exist per group for variance estimation
  filter(
    sum(Colony_Label == "surrounded") >= 2,
    sum(Colony_Label == "edge") >= 2
  ) %>%
  group_modify(~ broom::tidy(t.test(Area ~ Colony_Label, data = .x))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Condition, Set, Time, Biological_Replicate, Technical_Replicate, estimate_difference = estimate, statistic, p.value, parameter_df = parameter, conf.low, conf.high
  )

#Multiple testing correction (e.g., Benjamini-Hochberg FDR)
ttest_results_adjusted <- ttest_results %>%
  mutate(p.adj = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH")) 

# Using the ttest_results_adjusted dataframe from your code
ttest_results_adjusted  %>% filter(p.adj>0.05) %>% ggplot(aes(x = p.value, y = p.adj)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, color = "dodgerblue") +
  
  # Add a red dashed line where adjusted = unadjusted (y = x)
  # Points will fall above this line because adjusted p-values are larger
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  
  # Add dotted lines to show the 0.05 significance threshold
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dotted", color = "darkgray") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dotted", color = "darkgray") +
  
  # Add labels and format
  labs(
    title = "Adjusted vs. Unadjusted p-values",
    subtitle = "Comparing Raw p-values to Benjamini-Hochberg FDR",
    x = "Unadjusted p-value",
    y = "Adjusted p-value (FDR)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Export only the identifiers and p-values for a clean Prism import
ttest_results_csv <- ttest_results_adjusted %>%
  dplyr::select(Condition, Time, p.value, p.adj)

write.csv(ttest_results_csv, "output/t_test_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)

ttest_results_adjusted %>% filter(estimate_difference > 0 & p.adj < 0.05)
```

Coefficient of Variation Analysis 
```{r}
#calculate CV for all the data (not filtering anything out)
sd_cv_raw <- filtered_data %>% 
  group_by(Condition, Time, Strain) %>% 
  summarise(
    n_replicates = n(),
    mean_area    = mean(Area, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_area      = sd(Area, na.rm = TRUE),
    cv           = (sd_area / mean_area) * 100,
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(cv)) 

#Avg CV for all the data 
sd_cv_raw %>% summarize(mean(cv,na.rm=TRUE), median(cv,na.rm=TRUE))

#calculate CV for only the filtered data
sd_cv_retained <- filtered_data %>% 
  filter(Filter == "Passed") %>% 
  group_by(Condition, Time, Strain) %>% 
  summarise(
    n_replicates = n(),
    mean_area    = mean(Area, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_area      = sd(Area, na.rm = TRUE),
    cv           = (sd_area / mean_area) * 100,
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(cv)) %>% 
  mutate(QC_Group = "Retained (TRUE)")

#Avg CV for only the filtered data
sd_cv_retained %>% summarize(mean(cv,na.rm=TRUE), median(cv,na.rm=TRUE))

#calculate the cv for the flagged data 
sd_cv_flagged <- filtered_data %>% 
  filter(Filter != "Passed") %>% 
    group_by(Condition, Time, Strain) %>% 
  summarise(
    n_replicates = n(),
    mean_area    = mean(Area, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_area      = sd(Area, na.rm = TRUE),
    cv           = (sd_area / mean_area) * 100,
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(cv))  %>% 
  mutate(QC_Group = "Flagged Data")

#Avg CV for just the data that didn't pass filtering 
sd_cv_flagged %>% summarize(mean(cv,na.rm=TRUE), median(cv,na.rm=TRUE))
```
Now let's generate an Empirical Cumulative Distribution Function of the retained vs filtered data 
```{r}
# Combine both into one master data frame for plotting
combined_cv <- bind_rows(sd_cv_retained, sd_cv_flagged)

# 4. Generate ggplot ECDF Plot
ecdf_plot <- ggplot(combined_cv, aes(x = cv, color = QC_Group)) +
  stat_ecdf(geom = "step", linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Retained (TRUE)" = "#1f77b4", "Flagged Data" = "#d62728")) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 50), breaks = seq(0, 50, by = 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    x = "Coefficient of Variation (%)",
    y = "Cumulative Probability",
    color = "QC Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

# Display the plot in R / RStudio
print(ecdf_plot)

retained_cvs <- sd_cv_retained %>% pull(cv)
flagged_cvs  <- sd_cv_flagged  %>% pull(cv)

ecdf_retained_fn <- ecdf(retained_cvs)
ecdf_flagged_fn  <- ecdf(flagged_cvs)

x_grid <- seq(from = 0, to = 50, by = 0.1)

ecdf_table <- tibble(
  `CV_Percent_X`           = x_grid,
  `Blue_Line_Both_TRUE`   = ecdf_retained_fn(x_grid),
  `Red_Line_Both_Flagged` = ecdf_flagged_fn(x_grid)
)

write_csv(ecdf_table, "output/ECDF.csv")
```

Pearson's R 
Calculate Pearson's R for the unfiltered and filtered dataset 
```{r}
# 1. Generate all unique pairwise combinations of technical replicates
group_correlations <- filtered_data%>% 
  # Isolate each experimental group
  group_by(Condition, Time, Strain) %>%
  # Require at least 2 retained replicates to form a pair
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%
  # Generate all unique 2-way combinations of Shape_Area within each group
  summarise(
    pair_combos = list(as_tibble(t(combn(Area, 2)))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Flatten the list-column into individual rows
  unnest(pair_combos) %>%
  # Rename columns to represent paired observations
  rename(Rep_A = V1, Rep_B = V2)

group_correlations %>%
  summarise(
    total_pairs = n(),
    global_r    = cor.test(Rep_A, Rep_B, method = "pearson")$estimate,
    global_r2   = global_r^2,
    ci_lower    = cor.test(Rep_A, Rep_B, method = "pearson")$conf.int[1],
    ci_upper    = cor.test(Rep_A, Rep_B, method = "pearson")$conf.int[2],
    p_value     = cor.test(Rep_A, Rep_B, method = "pearson")$p.value
  )

# 1. Generate all unique pairwise combinations of technical replicates
group_correlations <- filtered_data%>% 
  filter(Filter == "Passed") %>% 
  # Isolate each experimental group
  group_by(Condition, Time, Strain) %>%
  # Require at least 2 retained replicates to form a pair
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%
  # Generate all unique 2-way combinations of Shape_Area within each group
  summarise(
    pair_combos = list(as_tibble(t(combn(Area, 2)))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Flatten the list-column into individual rows
  unnest(pair_combos) %>%
  # Rename columns to represent paired observations
  rename(Rep_A = V1, Rep_B = V2)

group_correlations %>%
  summarise(
    total_pairs = n(),
    global_r    = cor.test(Rep_A, Rep_B, method = "pearson")$estimate,
    global_r2   = global_r^2,
    ci_lower    = cor.test(Rep_A, Rep_B, method = "pearson")$conf.int[1],
    ci_upper    = cor.test(Rep_A, Rep_B, method = "pearson")$conf.int[2],
    p_value     = cor.test(Rep_A, Rep_B, method = "pearson")$p.value
  )
```
Generate a graph comparing replicates 
```{r}
# 1. Assign a random unique pair index (1 pair per colony, no overcounting)
sd_df_split_pairs <- filtered_data %>%
  filter(Filter == "Passed", !is.na(Area)) %>%
  group_by(Condition, Time, Strain) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%
  # Shuffle rows within each group
  slice_sample(prop = 1) %>%
  # Create pairs by grouping every 2 consecutive spots
  mutate(
    pair_id = ceiling(row_number() / 2),
    rep_label = if_else(row_number() %% 2 == 1, "Rep_A_Area", "Rep_B_Area")
  ) %>%
  group_by(Condition, Time, Strain, pair_id) %>%
  filter(n() == 2) %>% # Keep only complete pairs
  # Keep ONLY the grouping keys + pivoting columns so pivot_wider collapses properly
  dplyr::select(Condition, Time, Strain, pair_id, rep_label, Area) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = rep_label, values_from = Area) %>%
  ungroup()

paired_retained_plot <- ggplot(sd_df_split_pairs, aes(x = Rep_A_Area, y = Rep_B_Area)) +
  geom_pointdensity(method = "neighbors", size = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "magma") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 6000), labels = comma) + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 6000), labels = comma) +
  
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) 
# Display plot
paired_retained_plot

# Save high-res transparent PNG
ggsave(
  filename = "output/paired_retained_plot.png",
  plot = paired_retained_plot,
  width = 5,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "transparent"
)
```
